reuse.why: The change extends the existing schedule helpers and reuses getApproxNumberThreshold, although the budget template retains its own dispatch around the shared calculation.

duplication.why: Amount arithmetic is shared, but schedule-template.ts duplicates the helper's responsibility for deciding which operators require expected-amount calculation.

placement.why: Schedule amount policy remains in shared/schedules.ts, tolerance stays in shared/rules.ts, and API field projection belongs in api-models.ts.

scope.why: The edits are confined to schedule amount calculation, its consumers, focused tests, and release notes.

maintainability.why: Centralized arithmetic is sound, but optional operator propagation, caller-side dispatch, and retained midpoint documentation leave maintainers with an inconsistent calculation contract.

bypasses_abstraction.where: packages/loot-core/src/server/budget/schedule-template.ts conditionally invokes getExpectedAmount and handles other operators locally despite the helper already supporting plain numeric amounts.

disguised_duplication.where: schedule-template.ts replaces midpoint arithmetic with a helper call but preserves operator-based dispatch around it, duplicating part of the decision now owned by getExpectedAmount.

abstraction_drift.where: getExpectedAmount and getScheduledAmount each gain an optional op parameter, getExpectedAmount gains an isapprox branch, and schedule-template.ts partially bypasses the shared decision with its own operator dispatch.
